stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon by utilizing MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI inference speed.
This is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs directly on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: India's first privately-developed rocket reaches orbit on dramatic debut launch
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: India achieved a significant milestone with the successful orbital launch of its first privately-developed rocket.
The launch represents a major step forward in the growth and capability of the private space industry in India.
The success is highlighted by the sentiment of the involved personnel, indicating a breakthrough achievement.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program utilizes advanced satellites for wildfire detection.
The system is designed to identify wildfires that existing satellite technology overlooks.
The deployment is timely, addressing severe smoke and wildfire issues across the US and Canada.

stories.title: CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data
stories.author: Yunzhong He
bullet_points: Introduces CRAFT, a method to diagnose the underlying reasons for LLM failures, moving beyond simple performance measurement.
CRAFT converts rubric-based evaluation datasets into specific diagnoses of weak model capabilities.
The tool facilitates the generation of targeted fine-tuning data, enabling more effective model iteration and improvement.

stories.title: Harmonizing AI Safety Thresholds
stories.author: Markov Grey
bullet_points: Frontier AI companies use disparate capability thresholds, hindering third-party verification and cross-company comparison.
Lack of common minimum safety thresholds risks inconsistent risk mitigation and a 'race to the bottom' in AI safety.
The paper proposes a methodology to derive harmonized safety thresholds across three distinct risk domains (including misuse risks).

stories.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization
stories.author: Sasa Misailovic
bullet_points: Introduces PagedWeight, a novel method for efficiently serving Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses the memory tension in MoE serving between large model weights and growing KV caches.
Achieves efficiency by dynamically quantizing MoE model weights at runtime, balancing precision and cache size.

stories.title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
stories.author: Oleg Ruchayskiy
bullet_points: Introduces ShellFlow, a novel Riemannian conditional flow matching model for physics simulation.
The model uses a single transformer to learn the structure of the Standard Model across a vast energy range (sub-GeV to TeV).
It addresses a major limitation in current simulations by generating particles directly on their on-shell manifolds from LHC data.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning can introduce harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The study expands prior work by showing feasibility beyond limited data sources, accounting for large-scale and heterogeneous corpora and data curation pipelines.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for improved functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: A government pilot program is testing the use of Artificial Intelligence in insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the dual potential of AI: whether it can streamline or complicate the prior authorization process.
This addresses a significant, real-world application of AI in the complex healthcare and insurance sector.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
stories.author: Md Rayhanur Rahman
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) to process cybersecurity data.
The specific application is transforming unstructured threat information (like CVEs) into structured data for Autonomous Vehicle (AV) vulnerabilities.
This addresses a critical need for security practitioners to better analyze and manage risks within complex CAV ecosystems.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, comparing it against AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework significantly boosted validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The results suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage in this specific RL application, unlike high-rate AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current ML evaluation regarding 'active observation,' a key concept in human vision.
It posits that human vision is a continuous, hypothesis-driven closed loop, not a single snapshot.
The authors introduce ActiveVision, a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).

stories.title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
stories.author: Shuiwang Ji
bullet_points: The paper investigates when Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) outperform Single-Agent Systems (SAS) in complex tasks.
It applies an Information Bottleneck perspective to analyze the performance differences between MAS and SAS.
A key finding is the difference in context management: SAS uses a single shared context, while MAS uses isolated local contexts.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ToolSciVer, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
Addresses limitations in current methods, specifically struggling with locating visual evidence and interpreting scientific figures/tables.
Utilizes a tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning approach to integrate multimodal observations for reliable scientific reasoning.

stories.title: A Methodology for Auditable Trustworthiness Levels in AI Lifecycle Governance
stories.author: Andrea Ferrario
bullet_points: Proposes a lightweight methodology for assessing AI trustworthiness throughout its lifecycle.
Addresses the gap between high-level trustworthiness concepts and practical, lifecycle monitoring needs.
Focuses on creating transparent and contestable documentation for AI governance judgments.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM research by linking pretraining choices to the effectiveness of Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training.
Two key open questions are highlighted: how pretraining (size, data) influences RL returns, and the specific functional impact of RL on the model.
The study aims to overcome the difficulty of analyzing these interactions due to the vast and uncontrolled nature of standard LLM pretraining corpora.

stories.title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
stories.author: Andrea Manzoni
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency and high data requirements of standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) for control systems.
Proposes integrating physics knowledge into RL to improve control strategy synthesis for complex dynamical systems.
Aims to overcome limitations of RL in high-dimensional spaces, potentially enabling real-time optimal control.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, comparing it to AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework significantly boosted validation success (0.290 to 0.546).
The findings suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage in sparse-reward RL tasks over standard AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the concept of 'active observation' in human vision, where gaze is continuously redirected based on hypotheses.
It highlights that current vision-language benchmarks fail to empirically test whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) perform active observation.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to make active observation measurable for machine learning models.

stories.title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
stories.author: Hoang H. Nguyen
bullet_points: Introduces PRISA, a new LiDAR framework designed for proactive safety assessment at urban intersections.
Focuses on real-time monitoring to anticipate conflicts involving vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs).
Employs privacy-preserving and low-light-robust roadside sensors for long-term traffic observation.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific diagrams during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific infographics (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval evaluation (static document usefulness) fails when language models act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a retrieved document in agentic search depends on what it enables the agent to do next, not just its immediate relevance to the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static information retrieval metrics and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning capabilities in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses GI endoscopy case studies from MediaEval Medico 2025 to evaluate nine existing systems.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it doesn't guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in the AI models.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis in political conversations on TikTok.
Addresses the current limitation in computational analysis due to the scarcity of datasets that combine audiovisual information with conversational context.
The dataset is built from TikTok content related to the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering discussions about major political figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training priorities, leading to inefficiencies for later-added languages.
Adding new languages to existing LLMs can result in increased tokenization overhead, raising latency, compute, and energy costs.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding and LM-head matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of multilingual PLMs on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages due to tokenizer limitations.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed for Ge'ez-script languages (Amharic and Tigrinya).
Evaluates the model across 19 African languages, aiming to improve NLP capabilities for underrepresented linguistic communities.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
A key hurdle is the intractability of log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs, which existing methods approximate poorly.
The proposed work introduces 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients' to account for the sequential decision-making process during MDLM generation.

stories.title: Building Production-Grade LLM Evaluation Pipelines: From Vibes to Metrics
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on the practical engineering challenge of moving LLM evaluation from subjective assessment ('vibes') to quantifiable metrics.
Addresses the need for building robust, production-grade pipelines for Large Language Models.
Relevant to ML engineers and AI practitioners concerned with model reliability and quality assurance.

stories.title: Optimizing RAG at Scale: Chunking, Retrieval, and the Bayesian Search That Cut Latency 40%
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on practical optimization techniques for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
Highlights specific improvements in chunking and retrieval strategies for scalability.
Introduces a Bayesian Search method that resulted in a measurable 40% latency reduction.

stories.title: Optimizing RAG at Scale: Chunking, Retrieval, and the Bayesian Search That Cut Latency 40%
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for large-scale deployment.
Introduces a specific technical improvement: a Bayesian Search method.
Claims a significant performance gain, specifically a 40% reduction in latency.

bullet_points: Focuses on the practical engineering challenge of moving LLM evaluation from subjective assessment ('vibes') to quantifiable metrics.
Addresses the need for building robust, production-grade pipelines for Large Language Models.

stories.title: Building AI Agents That Don't Hallucinate: Structured Workflows, Guardrails, and Per-Step Evaluation
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on mitigating AI hallucination in autonomous agents.
Proposes solutions involving structured workflows and guardrails.
Highlights the importance of per-step evaluation for reliability.
